data.title: Georgia Social Media Star Allegedly Siphons $4,000,000 in Food Benefits Through 350+ Fake SNAP Accounts
data.description:
A Georgia social media personality is accused of stealing more than $4 million in food assistance benefits meant for low-income families.

The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia says Mercedes Reshard New, 39, of Atlanta, who goes by “Shawty Dred” online, allegedly controlled more than 350 fraudulent Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) accounts opened with stolen identities between January of 2020 and July of 2026.

Prosecutors say New had the EBT debit cards tied to those accounts mailed to addresses around metro Atlanta.

He also allegedly got his company, Shawty Dred LLC, approved as an authorized SNAP retailer and used its card reader to swipe more than $660,000 in benefits between April of 2024 and November of 2025.

The USDA pulled the store’s authorization in November 2025, and local police arrested New about two weeks later for allegedly selling SNAP benefits at a metro Atlanta store and seizing 14 EBT cards issued to other people.

Prosecutors say New then had replacement cards sent to his store and other Atlanta-area addresses.

In total, New allegedly tricked Georgia’s Division of Family & Children Services into loading about $4.6 million into the fake accounts, and roughly $4 million was drained.

Prosecutors say his Instagram account, which has more than two million followers, shows him flying on private jets, posing with Rolls-Royce and Maybach vehicles and holding large stacks of cash.

Says U.S. Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg,

“New allegedly stole over $4 million meant for poor families who need help putting food on the table. My office is fully committed to rooting out abuses of the SNAP program and holding accountable criminal con artists and scammers who appallingly seek to profit by stealing taxpayer money meant to feed vulnerable Americans.”

A federal grand jury indicted New on October 7th on 46 counts of mail fraud, 15 counts of aggravated identity theft and one count each of SNAP fraud and illegal transactions with access devices.

He was arrested on October 13th and is in U.S. Marshals Service custody.

data.title: Italy Dismantles Mafia-Linked Underground Bank Laundering $76,290,000 via Crypto
data.description:
Italian financial police are dismantling a mafia-linked underground bank that allegedly laundered tens of millions of euros through cryptocurrencies, fake invoices, and cross-border transfers.

The Guardia di Finanza of Milan and Monza Brianza in coordination with the Milan Anti-Mafia Directorate, targeted a network based in a car-rental business in Pero near Milan involving members of the ‘Ndrangheta groups in Crotone and the Casalesi Clan, reports Quartz.

The scheme collected illicit cash from drug trafficking and tax evasion before issuing over €110 million ($123.45 million) in false invoices through shell companies.

The shell companies issued invoices for services that were never provided, allowing businesses in industries such as logistics and construction to reduce their tax liabilities. After the companies wired payments, the network returned the money in cash, minus a fee. Couriers delivered the cash, which came from tax evasion and drug trafficking.

Money held in the shell companies’ bank accounts was transferred to lenders in Luxembourg, Lithuania and Germany before being routed through cryptocurrency exchanges and into digital wallets controlled by the organization.

Italian authorities arrested 30 people on Wednesday in an investigation into an alleged underground bank linked to organized crime. The suspects face accusations of belonging to a criminal organization, with alleged use of mafia-style methods serving as an aggravating factor. They allegedly sent about €68 million ($76.29 million) overseas, using digital assets to launder the illicit funds.

More than 350 officers participated in the operation, and authorities are moving to seize assets worth €21 million ($23.56 million). Spanish police are executing European arrest warrants, while Swiss authorities are working to apprehend another suspect.

data.title: Former Texas Bank Vice President Accused of Siphoning $193,810 From Customer Accounts and Arranging Loan To Benefit Himself
data.description:
A former bank executive in Texas faces a felony theft charge after allegedly diverting nearly $194,000 from customer accounts through unauthorized withdrawals and improper charges.

Josiah Kennedy worked as a vice president and lending officer at Citizens Bank in Abilene from February 2020 until he was fired on October 31st, 2023, reports KTXS.

Citizens Bank discovered the alleged activity after Kennedy’s firing, according to an affidavit.

The affidavit alleges that from January 2022 through October 2023, Kennedy directed employees to pull money from customer accounts, had clients billed for services they never received or withdrew funds without permission.

The money was allegedly deposited into accounts tied to Kennedy or sent by cashier’s check to P & P Services, an account the affidavit says he owned at First Financial Bank.

The affidavit also alleges he arranged a loan for another person that benefited him personally, with proceeds funding a cashier’s check to P & P Services and payments to his landscapers.

Citizens Bank estimated its loss at $193,810.90.

Court documents show the FBI contacted Abilene police about the case and that at least eight bank customers were affected, reports KTAB/KRBC.

Kennedy was booked into the Taylor County Jail on a felony theft charge and released after posting a $150,000 bond.

Kennedy previously agreed to be barred from the banking industry in a 2025 consent order with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, without admitting or denying wrongdoing.

data.title: Georgia Man and Florida Attorney Charged in Alleged Ponzi Schemes That Promised 16x Returns in Under Three Months
data.description:
A Georgia investment broker and a Florida attorney have been charged with running Ponzi schemes that allegedly took nearly $2 million from investors.

The schemes promised returns as high as 16 times an investment in as little as 30 to 90 days, says the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia.

Prosecutors say Roosevelt Tobias “Toby” Bailey, 70, of Duluth, ran two schemes through his company, Borg Global, from about October 2018 through October 2022.

The first, called the Micro-Cap program, promised to double investors’ money by pooling funds to buy precious stones and metals outside the US and resell them at a higher price inside the country.

The second, called the Standby Letter of Credit program, promised returns of up to 16 times the investment within 30 to 90 days.

Prosecutors allege the money was never used for either program.

Instead, the money allegedly went to Bailey’s personal and business accounts and to earlier investors to keep the schemes going.

Alvin Jones of Tampa, a former prosecutor and practicing attorney, allegedly routed investor money through his law firm’s trust accounts to Bailey and kept a portion for himself.

On September 22nd, a federal grand jury indicted Bailey on seven counts of wire fraud, one count of money laundering conspiracy and three counts of money laundering.

Jones faces one count of money laundering conspiracy and three counts of money laundering.

Bailey was arrested and arraigned on October 16th, and Jones was arrested and arraigned on October 20th.

Says U.S. Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg,

“Bailey allegedly lured investors based on promises of massive returns and false assurances that their investments would be held in Jones’s trust accounts. But instead of safeguarding that money, Jones allegedly funneled it to Bailey, keeping a piece for himself, while investors lost their savings.”

The FBI investigated the case with help from the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The charges are only allegations, and both men are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

data.title: South Dakota Woman Accused of Hiding Husband’s Death To Keep Collecting His Social Security Disability Payments
data.description:
A South Dakota woman is accused of hiding her husband’s death from the government so she could keep collecting his Social Security disability payments.

Beth Miley, 51, and her alleged accomplice, Jason Miley, 54, both of Pierre, have been indicted on charges of conspiracy to defraud the United States, conspiracy to commit bank fraud and bank fraud, says the U.S. Department of Justice.

Beth Miley is also charged with theft of government funds and Social Security fraud.

The indictment alleges she concealed the February 5th, 2023 death of her husband, a Social Security disability beneficiary, so she could keep receiving his monthly payments.

Prosecutors allege that between January 2024 and May of this year, the pair made monthly withdrawals of those payments from a bank account neither of them held or owned.

Court documents show Beth married Jason Miley in January 2024, nearly a year after her husband died, reports KELOLAND News.

Both defendants pleaded not guilty before U.S. Magistrate Judge Mark A. Moreno on October 15th and were released on bond.

Their trial is set for December 15th.

If convicted, they face up to 30 years in federal prison, a $250,000 fine, three years of supervised release and a $100 special assessment, and restitution may also be ordered.

Says Jacques Hansen, acting special agent-in-charge with the Social Security Administration’s Office of the Inspector General,

“The defendants are alleged to have concealed a beneficiary’s death to continue receiving Social Security disability benefits.”

The charges are accusations, and both defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

data.title: Chinese Prosecutors Seek Confiscation of 61,896 BTC Seized in UK From Massive Fraud: Report
data.description:
Chinese prosecutors are seeking to confiscate over 61,000 Bitcoin and related assets seized by UK authorities from a massive international fraud scheme.

The Tianjin No.2 Intermediate People’s Court accepted the application by the Tianjin Municipal People’s Procuratorate No.2 Branch on Sept. 28 to confiscate illegal proceeds including 61,896.41552945 BTC plus other virtual currencies, cash, jewelry, and financial assets.

The assets stem from a 2014-2017 Ponzi-style fraud run by the controller of a Tianjin company that raised over RMB 403.78 billion through false investment schemes, causing over RMB 199.77 billion in losses to more than 102,000 victims.

The perpetrator fled to the UK in 2017, where authorities seized the Bitcoin and related holdings valued at several billion pounds.

Prosecutors are applying to confiscate the property as illegal proceeds and fruits of the crime.

In the UK proceedings, the High Court ruled that Chinese law governs the existence and content of proprietary rights asserted by victims under POCA s.281.

A victim cannot necessarily recover cryptocurrency simply by proving that Bitcoin was bought with money taken from them.

Turner J held that Chinese law governs the existence and content of the proprietary rights asserted by the applicants.

No evidence on the content of Chinese law has yet been submitted, leaving the ownership battle ongoing.

The announcement period for interested parties runs six months from the 13th of October.

Source: The Paper

data.title: $6,520,000 Drained From First Horizon Customer’s Accounts After He’s Impersonated in Calls to the Bank, According to Lawsuit
data.description:
Scammers drained millions from a business owner’s bank accounts through a series of fraudulent wire transfers after impersonating him in phone calls to the lender.

Two of his companies allege in a lawsuit that First Horizon Bank permitted the transfers despite knowing about similar fraud involving other customers, says the law firm Fowler White Burnett.

Misael Rosario, 68, founded Century Metals and Supplies 38 years ago.

His companies, K&A Rosario Holdings LLC and MJR Fund I Inc., say they lost about $6.52 million through 15 unauthorized wires over three days in March.

According to the amended complaint, a caller contacted First Horizon on March 3rd claiming to have a new cellphone, and within minutes the accounts were allegedly accessed from an unfamiliar New York IP address.

Rosario’s attorney says the scammers verified their identity using publicly available information, reports WSOC-TV’s Action 9.

Law enforcement helped recover some of the money, but the companies are seeking more than $4.5 million that remains unreimbursed.

Says Rosario,

“We were totally in shock by the situation. A lot of that money was basically going to my grandkids and our future. I mean, eventually, I’m 68 years old. I got to retire eventually.”

The complaint alleges First Horizon had been notified in January of an earlier account takeover in which law firm Rabideau Klein says about $17.28 million was wired out of its trust account, with more than $6 million still missing.

The suit also alleges $2.29 million of Rosario’s companies’ money went to the same overseas recipient tied to that earlier incident.

Three pending Florida lawsuits collectively allege more than $24 million in unauthorized or fraudulent transfers between December 2025 and March.

Says attorney Victor Velarde,

“The allegations raise serious questions about what First Horizon knew following the earlier incidents and what measures were taken to protect customers from similar attacks.”

First Horizon says it has filed a motion for partial dismissal and intends to vigorously defend the case.

data.title: Ohio Law Firm Office Manager Accused of Stealing $864,380 From 11 Disabled Veterans, Including Purple Heart Recipient
data.description:
An Ohio law firm office manager is accused of stealing more than $864,000 from 11 disabled veterans whose money the firm was trusted to manage.

Darlene Toman, 64, faces six counts of bank fraud, six counts of wire fraud and four counts of aggravated identity theft, reports Military.com.

Federal prosecutors say she also took $77,051 from the pro bono account of Kabb Law Firm in Beachwood, where she worked.

The firm focuses on elder care and acts as a fiduciary for veterans who need help handling their finances because of injuries or disabilities tied to their military service.

One of the alleged victims is a veteran who received a Purple Heart after being shot in the head by a sniper in Iraq.

The indictment alleges Toman wrote checks to herself from client accounts and the firm’s pro bono account from February of 2018 to December of 2024.

Prosecutors say she spent most of the money on gambling and used some of it to pay off credit card debt.

Says the indictment,

“Rather than help veteran victims, defendant used their identities to steal from their bank accounts, stealing benefits that had been allocated to them, largely benefits intended to help veteran victims cover their basic living costs, often while they lived with disabilities derived from injuries suffered while serving their country in the U.S. Armed Services.”

Toman pleaded not guilty at her arraignment on Monday in U.S. District Court in Cleveland and was released on a $20,000 unsecured bond.

She started at the firm in 2010 through a work release program while serving a 60-day jail sentence for stealing about $12,000 from the Lake County Probate Court.

She was promoted to office manager in 2015 and held that job while the alleged scheme was underway.

data.title: JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo and Bank of America Detect Unauthorized AI Agents Accessing Customer Accounts: Report
data.description:
Major U.S. banks are moving to block AI agents after finding unauthorized bots working inside customer accounts.

Some of those agents have tried to take actions that appear to go beyond what account holders asked for, reports Axios, citing people familiar with the matter.

JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Bank of America and Morgan Stanley are among the banks scrambling to contain the risks agents pose.

In most cases, the agent gets in because the customer hands over their own username and password so an AI assistant can handle tasks for them.

Even with the customer’s permission, that breaks the rules at most banks, which require people to log in to their own accounts.

Bank executives are worried about what an agent with login access could do, especially if the user has given it the power to make purchases or move money.

Some banks have also tracked agents calling their customer service centers.

Bank executives describe the situation as horrifying, with one official saying the industry has grave concerns about agents getting into accounts and taking steps that could affect customers’ finances.

Morgan Stanley has started blocking third-party AI agents from its platforms, while JPMorgan, Bank of America and Citi are also restricting them.

A Morgan Stanley spokesperson says the bank has not seen instances of “rogue AI agents accessing our platforms.”

A Chase spokesperson says customers should not give their usernames and passwords to anyone.

Most banks have allowed, or are moving toward allowing, read-only access that lets agents see account information without taking any action, similar to what budgeting apps like Quicken already get.

data.title: Analyst Who Nailed 2026 Bitcoin Bottom Unveils the ‘Only Chart That Really Matters’ for BTC
data.description:
A widely followed crypto strategist is revealing what he believes is the only chart that matters for Bitcoin after BTC briefly went below $80,000 last week.

Pseudonymous analyst DonAlt tells his 797,800 followers on X that Bitcoin investors should look at BTC on a long-term timeframe to see its strength.

“If you zoom out a little bit, this is realistically the only chart that really matters.

Low timeframes may suck, but the monthly looks excellent still, especially considering all the geopolitical sh*t we’ve been getting thrown at us.”

DonAlt seems to suggest that BTC will remain bullish as long as it stays above $70,000.

On October 15th, Bitcoin fell to $79,732 before bouncing and rallying back toward $85,000. DonAlt notes that the recovery has put Bitcoin in the green for the month of October.

“You’d think the panic of the last week was more than the tiniest wick on the monthly candle.
Interesting how that works.

Think you all need to zoom out a bit more; save yourselves the stress (and money).”

He also says that Bitcoin continues to flash signs of strength despite geopolitical concerns.

“If this is all the pullback we’re getting, that’s incredible
Nice lil bounce off, honestly, a meh support
And all that amidst geopolitical turmoil and a broad expectation of a Black Monday

Good stuff; long may it last.”

In August of this year, DonAlt predicted Bitcoin would “explode” as it threatened to take out resistance at around $65,000.

At time of writing, Bitcoin is trading at $84,225.
